# Validation (M6) — current status

**Read this first.** Every number below comes from **synthetic** documents generated by `src/taadeel/synthetic.py` with known operations. They measure whether the engine recovers operations it was given. They do **not** measure accuracy on real UAE legislation. A hand-checked real gold set (cited per item) is **not yet built** because no source currently permits text collection (see `DATA_SOURCES.md`). Until it exists, claims about real-world accuracy must not be made.

Reproduce: `python -m taadeel.validate table 30` (seeds 0–29 per scenario; 40 articles per document; operations per document: 5 replace, 3 repeal, 3 insert (1 «مكرر»), 2 orthography-only, unless noted).

| scenario | align acc. | forced on repealed (high-conf / any) | replaced P / R | repealed P / R | inserted P / R |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| easy (random text, small edits) | 1.000 | 0 / 0 of 90 | 1.000 / 1.000 | 1.000 / 1.000 | 1.000 / 1.000 |
| templated near-duplicates, small edits | 0.981 | 1 / 30 of 90 | 0.751 / 0.987 | 0.968 / 0.667 | 1.000 / 0.689 |
| templated, 40% of words edited | 0.963 | 0 / 31 of 90 | 0.650 / 0.867 | 0.967 / 0.656 | 0.721 / 0.489 |
| templated, 70% of words edited | 0.918 | 0 / 32 of 90 | 0.511 / 0.593 | 0.604 / 0.644 | 0.417 / 0.444 |
| templated, many inserts/repeals | 0.877 | 0 / 150 of 240 | 0.446 / 0.896 | 0.989 / 0.375 | 1.000 / 0.379 |

## What this shows

1. **The easy scenario is uninformative.** Perfect scores arise because random text from a large word pool makes articles trivially distinguishable. It stays only as a sanity check.
2. **Near-duplicate articles are the real difficulty.** When articles share most of their wording (templated text, which resembles boilerplate-heavy statutes), a repealed article is often matched to a similar neighbour. Without the ambiguity check, 103 of 300 repealed articles were force-matched (seeds 0–99). With it, those pairs are marked `low` confidence (31 of 90 in seeds 0–29), so high-confidence forced matches fall to about 1 of 90 in this scenario. They are still *aligned*, so recall for `repealed` and `inserted` drops (0.38–0.69): the engine reports them as `replaced` with low confidence instead of repealed + inserted.
3. **Heavy rewrites degrade alignment.** At 70% of words edited, precision for `inserted` falls to 0.42 and `replaced` to 0.51. Text similarity cannot distinguish a heavily rewritten article from a repeal plus an unrelated insertion; structural position helps only partly.
4. **A single score threshold is not the fix.** A sweep of `T_LOW` (0.35–0.65) on held-out seeds (1000–1059) only traded alignment accuracy and recall for modestly fewer forced matches (for example, mean `replaced` recall fell from 0.82 to 0.50 while forced matches fell from 479 to 301). The sweep timed out before 0.75 and 0.85, so those values were not evaluated.

## Caveats on these numbers

* The ambiguity margin (0.05) was introduced **after** seeing results on seeds 0–99 and 1000–1059. The table is therefore not a clean held-out estimate; it documents behaviour after a design change motivated by observed failures.
* Thresholds `T_MATCH=0.60`, `T_LOW=0.35` are not calibrated on real text.
* Synthetic text is random Arabic word sequences; it does not model legal drafting, cross-references, or amendment-by-reference language.
* Point-in-time correctness is covered only by unit tests on hand-built timelines (`tests/test_engine.py`), not by an evaluation set.
* Moves of an article to a distant position are not supported (monotonic alignment); they surface as repeal + insert. No test of this limitation has been scored.

## Adversarial cases covered by unit tests

Pure renumbering; «مكرر» articles; orthography-only change (diacritics, Arabic-Indic digits) classified `clarified`; a numeric change (30 → 60) classified `replaced` and never `clarified`; dissimilar articles with the same number staying unaligned; schema rejects missing provenance and mislabeled synthetic data.

## Required next step to make validation meaningful

Build `data/gold/` from laws with documented amendment histories, hand-checked against the official text, each item citing its source. Candidates are listed in `RESEARCH.md` §4. This needs permission to store and use the text (see `DATA_SOURCES.md`).
